user.title: Arr Stack — Global Settings
user.description: Optional global settings that apply to all services.

data_description.skip_ssl_verify: Enable if any of your services use self-signed certificates or are behind a reverse proxy with an untrusted cert. Leave disabled for normal setups.
data_description.debug_logging: Logs every proxy request (URL, response status/body) to the Home Assistant log at DEBUG level. Enable when reporting a bug, then disable again afterwards.

service_selection.title: Arr Stack — Select Services
service_selection.description:
Choose which optional services you want to configure. Only the selected steps will be shown.

**Media (Radarr + Sonarr) is always required** and will always be configured first.

torrents.title: Arr Stack — Torrent Clients
torrents.description: All clients are optional — fill in only the one you use.

qbittorrent.name: qBittorrent
qbittorrent.description: Active torrents in the card, with pause, resume and delete. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.qbittorrent_user: The username you use to log into the qBittorrent Web UI
data_description.qbittorrent_password: The password for the qBittorrent Web UI

deluge.name: Deluge
deluge.description: Alternative to qBittorrent. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.deluge_password: Deluge Web UI password, set in Preferences → Interface

rtorrent.name: rTorrent / ruTorrent
rtorrent.description: Alternative to qBittorrent. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.rtorrent_url: e.g. http://192.168.1.10:9080 — base URL of ruTorrent, XMLRPC at /RPC2
data_description.rtorrent_user: HTTP Basic auth username for ruTorrent, if configured in nginx
data_description.rtorrent_password: HTTP Basic auth password for ruTorrent

gluetun.name: Gluetun
gluetun.description: VPN status and the forwarded port for the torrent client. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.gluetun_url: e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8000 — the HTTP control server, default port 8000
data_description.gluetun_api_key: API key defined in /gluetun/auth/config.toml. Leave empty if auth is disabled.

usenet.title: Arr Stack — Usenet Clients
usenet.description: Both clients are optional — fill in only the one you use.

sabnzbd.name: SABnzbd
sabnzbd.description: Usenet queue and history in the card, with retry and delete. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.sabnzbd_api_key: Find it in SABnzbd → Config → General → API Key

nzbget.name: NZBGet
nzbget.description: Alternative to SABnzbd. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.nzbget_user: NZBGet Control username, default is nzbget

media.title: Arr Stack — Media
media.description: Radarr and Sonarr are the core of the card and are required.

radarr.name: Radarr
radarr.description: Movie library, download status and interactive search. Required.

data_description.radarr_api_key: Find it in Radarr → Settings → General → API Key

sonarr.name: Sonarr
sonarr.description: TV library, download status and interactive search. Required.

data_description.sonarr_api_key: Find it in Sonarr → Settings → General → API Key

quality.title: Arr Stack — 2nd instances
quality.description: Optional second instances of Radarr and Sonarr, typically the 4K ones.

radarr2.name: Radarr — second instance
radarr2.description: A separate Radarr, typically the 4K one. The card lets you pick the instance when adding a movie. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.radarr2_api_key: Find it in your second Radarr → Settings → General → API Key

sonarr2.name: Sonarr — second instance
sonarr2.description: A separate Sonarr, typically the 4K one. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.sonarr2_api_key: Find it in your second Sonarr → Settings → General → API Key

discovery.title: Arr Stack — Discovery
discovery.description: Where the card gets posters, metadata and requests from. Everything here is optional.

tmdb.name: TMDB — needed by 1 September 2026 if you do not use Seerr
tmdb.description: Only needed when Seerr is not configured. With a Seerr URL filled in below, the discovery rows, search and title details all come from Seerr and you can ignore this section. Otherwise, fill in your own TMDB API key before 1 September 2026 — after that date the posters, ratings, cast, trailers and the Trending and Popular rows stop working without one.

data_description.tmdb_api_key: Without Seerr this key powers posters, ratings, cast, trailers and the Trending/Popular rows. Get one free at themoviedb.org → Settings → API — it takes a minute and no payment details are needed. Required from 1 September 2026.

seerr.name: Seerr
seerr.description: Requests, discovery rows and search. Optional — without it, movies and shows are added straight to Radarr and Sonarr. Seerr is the merged successor to Overseerr and Jellyseerr; both of those work here too.

data_description.seerr_api_key: Find it in Seerr → Settings → General → API Key

family.name: Family account
family.description: A non-admin Seerr account for family members. The card uses it to show and withdraw their own requests. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.seerr_family_email: The login email of that Seerr account

guest.name: Guest account
guest.description: A second non-admin Seerr account for guests. Map Home Assistant users to it in the card editor. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.seerr_guest_email: The login email of that Seerr account

bazarr.name: Bazarr
bazarr.description: Subtitle status per movie and show. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.bazarr_api_key: Find it in Bazarr → Settings → General → API Key

plex.name: Plex
plex.description: Playback control from the card. Follow the authentication link above, then submit.

data_description.plex_server_url: Leave empty to auto-detect. Fill in only when auto-detection picks the wrong address — for example when Home Assistant runs on a different machine or VLAN than Plex.

emby.name: Emby
emby.description: Alternative to Plex. Leave empty to skip.

jellyfin.title: Arr Stack — Streaming Stats
jellyfin.description: All three are optional — fill in the one matching your media server.

tautulli.name: Tautulli
tautulli.description: Streaming statistics for Plex. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.tautulli_url: e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8181, or http://192.168.1.10:8181/tautulli behind a subpath — default port is 8181
data_description.tautulli_api_key: Find it in Tautulli → Settings → Web Interface → API Key

jellystat.name: Jellystat
jellystat.description: Streaming statistics for Jellyfin. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.jellystat_api_key: Find it in Jellystat → Settings → API Key

tracearr.name: Tracearr (beta)
tracearr.description: Watch history and storage statistics across Plex, Jellyfin and Emby. Beta — leave empty to skip. Besides the URL and API key, fill in the session cookie: the statistics and library screens need it.

data_description.tracearr_api_key: Find it in Tracearr → Settings → API Key
data_description.tracearr_refresh_token: Older login method, kept for accounts that already have one. Prefer the session cookie — the refresh token is being retired and will stop working.
data_description.tracearr_session_cookie: Needed for watch history, library and storage statistics — the API key alone cannot reach those. Open Tracearr in your browser while signed in, press F12 → Application → Cookies, and copy the whole better-auth.session_token entry (name and value).

trakt.name: Trakt.tv
trakt.description: Fills the Trakt Recommended category in the card. Trakt VIP is required: since July 2026 only VIP members can register an API application, and applications belonging to free accounts were removed, so an old Client ID now answers 403. Without VIP leave both fields empty and the card hides this category. With VIP, create an application at https://trakt.tv/oauth/applications/new — any name, redirect URI urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob — and copy its Client ID and Client Secret into the fields below.

data_description.trakt_client_id: From Trakt → Settings → Apps → API Applications. Leave empty to skip Trakt.
data_description.trakt_client_secret: From the same Trakt application page. Needed only when a Client ID is filled in.

suggestarr.name: SuggestArr
suggestarr.description: Fills the SuggestArr category in the card. This is a category of its own, not a replacement for Trakt — you can run both, either, or neither. SuggestArr is free and self-hosted and needs no third-party account: it reads what you actually watched on Plex, Jellyfin or Emby and suggests titles you do not own yet. See https://github.com/giuseppe99barchetta/SuggestArr. Leave the fields empty to skip it.

data_description.suggestarr_url: Address of the SuggestArr web interface, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:5001. Leave empty to skip SuggestArr.
data_description.suggestarr_user: The same login you use for the SuggestArr web interface. Leave empty if SuggestArr runs with AUTH_MODE=local_bypass or disabled — then Home Assistant is trusted by its local network and no login is needed.
data_description.suggestarr_password: Password for that login. Leave empty for the same reason as the username.

trakt_poll.title: Arr Stack — Trakt authorisation
trakt_poll.description:
Open **{verify_url}** and enter code:

# `{user_code}`

Once you have authorised the app on Trakt, click **Submit** to complete setup.

prowlarr.name: Prowlarr
prowlarr.description: Indexer management and search statistics. Leave empty to skip.

data_description.prowlarr_api_key: Find it in Prowlarr → Settings → General → API Key

maintainerr.name: Maintainerr
maintainerr.description: Rules and collections for automatic media cleanup. Maintainerr has no authentication, so only the URL is needed. Leave empty to skip.

metrics.title: Metrics collection
metrics.description:
You made it all the way to the end of the setup — so you have seen how much work went into this card. To keep improving it I need to know which parts people actually use, so the card sends one anonymous ping: the card version, whether it runs on a phone, and which services are configured (just the names — no URLs, no API keys, no titles, nothing about your library). The installation is identified by a short hash of your dashboard's hostname, so I cannot tell who you are, and the data cannot be traced back to you.

You can see for yourself what is collected: https://argalas.org/arr-stats

If you would still rather not take part, that is completely fine — your privacy is yours. Turn the switch below on and this installation stops sending anything.

data.metrics_opt_out: Don't send metrics from this installation

data_description.metrics_opt_out: Leave it off to keep helping the project. Switch it on and this installation stops sending anything.
